rationale: Roberts is most likely to keep the majority together with a narrow, record-bound opinion allowing an inclusive “any-part Black” measure when consistently applied and treating metric-switching as an evidentiary/clear-error issue rather than a categorical rule. Thomas and/or Alito are likely to dissent on administrability and the need for an objective Gingles I threshold, while one or more textualist-leaning joiners (especially Gorsuch/Kavanaugh/Barrett) may write separately to emphasize limits and consistency requirements.
